cause_plain: The app crashes at startup. A route is declared with status 204 (No Content), and its function has a return type such as `-> dict`. FastAPI treats that return type as the response body, and 204 responses can't have a body.
real_cause: get_typed_annotation() turned the string annotation 'None' (from postponed annotations) into NoneType rather than None, so the route was treated as having a response body and the 204 assertion failed.

cause_plain: Passing a URL value named "self" to url_for crashes with a TypeError instead of building the URL. This is because the method's own "self" argument has the same name as the value.
real_cause: Flask.url_for() declared self as an ordinary parameter, so a URL value named 'self' passed via **values collided with it; the fix makes self positional-only.

cause_plain: A POST that gets redirected (301, 302 or 303) is turned into a GET with no body. The new request still says it has a body, so the client fails and the request hangs and then times out.
real_cause: RedirectMiddleware.redirect_headers() kept Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding when a redirect switched the method to GET and dropped the body, so h11 saw too little data for the declared length.

cause_plain: Defining a class with `@define` crashed with a SyntaxError. The class has a `__attrs_pre_init__` that takes arguments, plus keyword-only fields that have defaults. attrs wrote broken code for the `__init__` it generates, and Python refused to compile it.
real_cause: _attrs_to_init_script() built the __attrs_pre_init__ call from kw_only argument strings that still included '=default', generating invalid code like a=attr_dict['a'].default=a=....

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a file that has a multi-line string. It checks whether the line is short enough and reads a nesting-depth value that some pieces of code never get. The run stops with an internal error instead of formatting the file.
real_cause: blib2to3 Leaf declared bracket_depth only as an annotation and neither __init__ nor clone() set it, so leaves created outside the bracket tracker lacked the attribute that is_line_short_enough() reads.
